videos.title: How Food Choices Shape Memory, Cognition & Cravings | Dr. Scott Kanoski
videos.description:
Dr. Scott Kanoski, PhD, is a Professor of Human and Evolutionary Biology and Neurobiology at the University of Southern California. We discuss how different foods impact memory and cognitive function as well as cravings. We also discuss how GLP-1 drugs work to control hunger in the brain and body, the role of the gut microbiome, and the effects of artificial and low calorie sweeteners on hunger and satiety. This episode highlights how nutrition impacts much brain health and learning capacity and how our memory impacts food choices too.

videos.title: Elon musk vs Ambani | starlink vs jio 🤯
videos.description:
Elon Musk vs Mukesh Ambani: The Starlink India Battle Explained 🇮🇳

Elon Musk has publicly accused powerful Indian business interests of blocking Starlink’s entry into India. In a series of posts on X in early October 2026, he called out “oligarchs,” asked “Is Ambani the real boss of India?”, and even sarcastically addressed Mukesh Ambani as “Prime Minister Ambani.”

In this video, we break down:
- What Musk actually said
- Why Starlink is still not live in India
- The government’s response
- How Jio, Airtel, and OneWeb fit into the picture
- What this means for internet access in remote areas of India

**Key Tweets by Elon Musk:**

Oligarchs accusation (7 Oct 2026):  
https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2107854307077034294

“Is Ambani the real boss of India?” (8 Oct 2026):  
https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2108187065687118261

“Dear Prime Minister Ambani” (9 Oct 2026):  
https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2108604227643719745

Competition & pricing post (10 Oct 2026):  
https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2108994867582095465

**Other Useful Resources:**

- BBC: Why Elon Musk is taking on India’s richest man over Starlink  
  https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvglw9ryjrylo

- TechCrunch: Musk intensifies attack on Ambani  
  https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/09/elon-musk-intensifies-attack-on-ambani-over-starlink-india-launch-delay/

- Reuters: India rejects monopoly claim  
  https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/india-rejects-monopoly-claim-after-musk-accuses-ambani-blocking-starlink-launch-2026-10-09/

- Economic Times coverage of the oligarchs claim and government reply

**Context:**  
Starlink has spent years complying with Indian regulations and already holds key licences, but final security clearance and spectrum allocation are still pending. Jio Satellite and OneWeb are in a similar position. The government maintains the process is fair and non-discriminatory.

What do you think — should Starlink be allowed to compete in India? Drop your views in the comments.

People in October 1965. India was facing a crisis.
We had just fought a war with Pakistan, and the Prime Minister of India made a request to the nation that no Prime Minister should ever have to make.
Lal Bahadur Shastri asked every Indian to give up one meal a week. His exact words were "Sacrifice one meal at least a week!"
Why??
Because India simply did not have enough food. By 1966, an average of three American ships a day were docking at Indian ports with grain, and Economists called India a "ship-to-mouth" economy.
61 years later, Dr Jaishankar is warning us about a major food crisis!!
Now, the moment this clip went viral, a lot of people thought India is going to run out of food?
But you know what?? India today is sitting on so much rice that a Chief Minister is begging the Centre to take it away because there's no space left to store it.
So the question is, how can a country drowning in grain be staring at a food crisis?
Well, Jaishankar’s warning does not start in a godown. It starts in a 45 kilo bag, on a ship and in a 39 kilometre wide strip of water between Iran and Oman.
And at the very end of this video, I'll tell you about one sentence uttered by Indira Gandhi in 1966, after a phone call with the President of the United States. That one sentence tells you the future of India!!
So in this video, let's answer three questions:
What exactly did Dr Jaishankar say, and why is a foreign minister talking about food?
